newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr breaks through 1.67 marks, bourses soft.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr breaks through 1.67 marks, bourses soft.

text.p: The dollar surged through the 1.67 mark level on Tuesday, shrugging off weekend signals from the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations that it had risen far enough.
Despite afternoon profit-taking, dealers said it was well bid and holding at about 1.6710 at 1530 gmt, just down from a 1.6734 peak hit in early afternoon -- its highest level since June, 1994 .
On the bourses, leading European shares received a little late encouragement when Wall Street opened higher and quickly firmed by about a quarter of a percentage point .

However, It was not enough to move London or Paris out of the negative territory they had languished in for most of the day caused by predictable mark downs following a 49 point slide in the Dow overnight.
Frankfurt was an exception, where the stronger dollar -- favourable for German exports -- managed to outweigh the overnight New York weakness and stocks closed bourse trading slightly higher.

Currency traders said the dollar's climb was supported by continuing worries about the German economy. The dollar was also firm against the yen, but fears of possible intervention by the Bank of Japan to curb its rise were having a damping effect.
Last weekend a statement from G7 finance chiefs said currency "misalignments" had now been corrected, but it shunned talk of intervention to hold the dollar down.
"Japanese officials will continue to talk a stable yen, but I think the dollar will remain pretty well underpinned near term," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.,
Against the yen, the U. S. currency was trading at around 122.90 in mid-afternoon, off the day's highs and only slightly up from late Monday's 122.83.
"The market's concluding, and I think rightly so, that G7 was not an absolute, definitive watershed," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
"So long as the G7 is not going to change its monetary policy, the dollar is likely to push higher."

It was not only against the dollar that the mark was weak -- sterling romped to a fresh 52-month high of 2.7460 marks despite indications that UK interest rates are on hold, at least for the time being.

The London stock market, Europe's busiest, remained weak despite the firmer opening in New York. Its blue chip FTSE 100 index was trading down a quarter of a percent in late afternoon, not far off its lows of the day.

Recent evidence that UK inflationary pressures are modest continued to underpin the market's conviction that UK interest rates will not be increased soon and the favourable interest rate picture has convinced some strategists that the FTSE's five percent advance so far this year has further to go before any significant correction.
In Frankfurt the DAX index of leading shares closed up 3.22 points at 3187.58 after a day of low trading volumes due to Tuesday being a half-day pre-Lent holiday.
In Paris French stocks managed to open higher but quickly fell into negative territory, where they remained hardly moved by the higher start in New York.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down nearly half a percent at 1530 gmt. Despite the losses, traders said the French market was underpinned to some degree by firmness in bond prices and in the dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6710 marks and 122.90 yen compared with 1.6571 marks and 122.83 yen in late European trading on Monday
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 10.7 at 4,297.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 13.13 at 2,582.24.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 3.22 at 3,187. 58
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $339.40. Silver was at $4.93.
